title: Verifier-first contrast
abstract: A synthetic conditional object that uses state-positive, state-negative, inactive-intervention, and burden-matched contrasts to separate target-state dependence from broad burden.
disposition_reason: The contrasts are useful only after the target-context state can be measured.
nearest_prior_art: General inactive and burden-matched control architectures.
strongest_reason: It can distinguish the intended route from broad burden.
weakest_causal_edge: The state-positive and state-negative conditions may differ in uncontrolled ways.
pairwise_summary: Not pairwise-ranked; it supports the primary decision rather than competing with it.
reviewer_disagreement: Reviewers disagree on whether burden matching is sufficient.
reviewer_critiques: State contrasts must be interpreted independently of broad burden.
reentry_condition: Use after the target-context gate has an operational measurement.
scientific_summary: A verifier-first contrast defines the controls needed before a route-specific claim can be made.
causal_mechanism: Matched controls isolate target-state dependence from inactive intervention and broad burden.
evidence_basis: Synthetic falsification logic and control-design principles.
next_discriminating_experiment: Compare state-positive, state-negative, inactive-intervention, and burden-matched conditions with a route-specific readout.
